text:
Haru

Model ·
Technical blog ·
Technical blog (Japanese)

Haru is a low-latency and multilingual full-duplex spoken dialogue model: it
listens and speaks at the same time, the way people do on a phone call. This
repository contains the inference code for Haru-4B , a pretrained base
model, with three implementations and a web demo.

- Native full-duplex at 7.5 Hz. Every 133 ms the model takes one frame of
 the user's audio and produces one frame of its own audio and text. User
 audio, model audio and model text are summed into a single position of the
 language model, so listening and speaking never wait for each other.
- Continuous audio, one sampling step. Audio is a 64-dimensional latent
 per frame. A small MLP head with MeanFlow sampling produces it in one step
 from the language model's hidden state; there is no separate audio
 transformer and there are no discrete audio tokens.
- Character and voice control. A text card sets the character, a short
 reference clip sets the voice.
- Multilingual. English, Spanish, Portuguese, German, French, Chinese,
 Japanese, Russian and Korean.

 How it works

 
 
 

- The text stream carries the model's words in chunks. Frames without text
 hold a padding token, and an end-of-padding token on the frame before the
 model starts to speak.
- The audio codec is the causal VibeVoice acoustic tokenizer: 24 kHz audio
 to and from one latent per 3200 samples.
- The prompt is the character card as a system turn, followed by the voice
 reference as audio on the model's stream.

 Repository

 Directory What it is 
 --- --- 
 haru/ PyTorch implementation, web demo server, offline inference 
 haru mlx/ MLX implementation for Apple silicon, with a native macOS app 
 haru vllm/ Plugin that serves Haru with vLLM-Omni 
 client/ Web client of the demo (React); a built copy ships inside haru 

All three read the same checkpoint,
 higurashi-ai/Haru-4B .

 Quick start

With an NVIDIA GPU (about 12 GB of memory):

 

Open , pick a character, give the model a voice, and
talk. A browser only gives a page microphone access on localhost or over
HTTPS.

For low latency, we recommend wired headphones and a wired microphone.
Bluetooth devices add 100 ms or more.

To let someone else try it, add --share ( pip install -e "./haru[share]" ): the
server prints a public HTTPS link that tunnels to it. Anyone with the link can
use the demo, and the traffic passes through Gradio's share servers.

 Bring your own voice. Haru ships without voice clips. In the demo, upload
or record a clip of the voice the model should speak with: one speaker, 3
seconds to 3 minutes, clean speech. In Python, pass it as reference . Only
use voices you have the right to use.

To give the demo a default voice, save a clip as
 haru/haru/assets/voices/ .flac ( en.flac , ja.flac , ...) and
restart the server: the demo then offers it as the default voice of that
language. Without the file, the demo does not show the option.

 Python

 

The model is one frame ahead of the user: start() returns frame 0, and each
 step() with user frame k returns model frame k + 1 .

 The system prompt

Haru reads its character from a card with a fixed layout. Build one with render card :

 

 Offline

 

 Serving with vLLM-Omni

For many concurrent conversations and the lowest latency on a GPU server, see
 haru vllm/ . The web demo can use it as its engine:

 

 Custom kernels

The hot paths of a frame have hand-written kernels, alongside plain
implementations that give the same results:

 Where Kernel What it speeds up 
 --- --- --- 
 haru (NVIDIA GPUs) Triton kernels replayed from CUDA graphs ( haru/haru/codec triton ) The audio codec: about 0.7 ms instead of 6 ms to encode or decode a frame. Opt-in with DuplexConfig(codec backend="triton") or --codec-backend triton 
 haru vllm The same Triton codec, used automatically Audio encode and decode inside the engine step 
 haru mlx (Apple silicon) Metal kernels ( gated delta.py , vibevoice codec.py ) The Gated DeltaNet recurrence of the language model and the depthwise convolutions of the codec 

 Limitations

Haru-4B is a pretrained base model, released for research. It holds a natural
conversation, but it is not a reliable source of facts and does not follow
instructions the way an assistant does. It can imitate the voice of a
reference clip; only use voices you have the right to use.

 License

The code and the Haru-4B weights are released under the Apache License 2.0.
See THIRD PARTY NOTICES.md for the third-party work
they include.

 Acknowledgments

Haru builds on the work of many open-source projects. We are grateful to their
authors and communities.

- Qwen — the Qwen3.5 language model that Haru-4B
 starts from.
- VibeVoice — the causal acoustic
 tokenizer Haru uses as its audio codec, and the idea of next-latent
 generation at 7.5 Hz.
- Moshi — the pioneering full-duplex
 speech model. Our web client is derived from the Moshi web client.
- Improved MeanFlow — the one-step
 generative modeling framework behind the audio head.
- vLLM and
 vLLM-Omni — the serving engine
 and its full-duplex realtime framework, which haru vllm plugs into.
- MLX,
 mlx-lm and
 mlx-audio — the array framework and
 the model code haru mlx builds on.

install.title: Quick start
install.html:
With an NVIDIA GPU (about 12 GB of memory):

pip install -e ./haru
python -m haru.server --hf-repo higurashi-ai/Haru-4B

Open http://localhost:8998, pick a character, give the model a voice, and talk. A browser only gives a page microphone access on localhost or over HTTPS.

For low latency, we recommend wired headphones and a wired microphone. Bluetooth devices add 100 ms or more.

To let someone else try it, add --share (pip install -e "./haru[share]"): the server prints a public HTTPS link that tunnels to it. Anyone with the link can use the demo, and the traffic passes through Gradio's share servers.

Bring your own voice. Haru ships without voice clips. In the demo, upload or record a clip of the voice the model should speak with: one speaker, 3 seconds to 3 minutes, clean speech. In Python, pass it as reference. Only use voices you have the right to use.

To give the demo a default voice, save a clip as haru/haru/assets/voices/<language>.flac (en.flac, ja.flac, ...) and restart the server: the demo then offers it as the default voice of that language. Without the file, the demo does not show the option.

On a Mac with Apple silicon, build the native app (see haru_mlx/swift):

cd haru_mlx
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e .
cd swift && ./build_app.sh        # then open build/Haru.app
